overall_summary: Analysis of 47 unique shorts across multiple scraping passes reveals extreme exoplanet and cinematic cosmic survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') massively outperform all other verticals. Videos featuring immersive planetary descent hooks consistently generated 800-1,000+ views with peak like-to-view ratios (~3.7%), while psychology and repetitive trivia (e.g., octopus hearts, earworms, brain memory tricks) consistently flopped below 100 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person 'What If You Fell Into...' Extreme Planetary Descents
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) achieved top-tier engagement and retention.
winning_patterns.action: Standardize the high-peril first-person perspective hook combined with surreal cosmic environmental physics.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' reached 980 views and 21 likes within 9 days, driving the highest recent views-per-day velocity (~108 V/D).
winning_patterns.action: Lead with immediate paradigm-shifting scale or temporal paradoxes within the opening 1.5 seconds.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' posted across multiple iterations stalled at 5, 10, and 53 views; 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' gained only 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Halt generic psychology and abstract brain trivia; viewers fail to convert on static text-and-stock-footage intros.

weak_patterns.evidence: Duplicate uploads of 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (118 to 363 views) yielded low interaction velocity compared to space survival content.
weak_patterns.action: Eliminate low-effort trivia reposts in favor of rich narrative micro-storytelling.

next_video.concept: What If You Stepped Onto a Neutron Star?
next_video.opening_direction: Instantly plunge the viewer from orbit toward an ultra-dense pulsar spinning 700 times per second, stating that a single teaspoon weighs more than Mount Everest.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that before your boot even touches the crust, gravitational tidal forces would stretch your atoms into microscopic noodles, vaporizing you into pure energy in a fraction of a millisecond.
next_video.reason: The 21-second 'What If You Fell Into...' format represents the channel's strongest engagement cluster (800-1,000+ views), and a neutron star is an unexploited, high-stakes extreme cosmic topic that fits this proven audience demand.

Do not use recycled trivia questions about shark ages or space silence
Must focus specifically on neutron star density and spaghettification

experiment: Test opening with an immediate high-stakes acoustic SFX impact and a tactile question ('What would happen to your body if you touched a neutron star?') versus purely visual exoplanet names to evaluate first-3-second retention.
